orders.text:
SA No. 41 of 2009 
Hon'ble Prafulla C. Pant, J.
 
Heard Sri Sharad Sharma, Senior Advocate, assisted by Sri C.S. 
Rawat, learned counsel for the appellant and perused the impugned 
judgment and decree dated 30.04.2009, passed by the first appellate 
court (Additional District Judge / Fast Track Court V, Dehradun), in 
Civil Appeal No. 5 of 2008. 
Admit the appeal on following substantial question of law:- 
Whether the act on the part of the counsel (Sri J.M. Singhal) who 
appeared earlier on behalf of appellant (plaintiff) in the suit and 
thereafter the said counsel appeared on behalf of respondent at the 
stage of first appeal, vitiated the entire proceedings before the first 
appellate court? 
Issue notices to respondent-Ram Niwas Goel. 
Having heard learned counsel for the appellant and after going 
through the impugned judgment and decree passed by the courts 
below, as an interim measure it is directed that respondent shall not 
create third party interest in respect of the 50% share in the property 
purchased through registered sale deed dated 23.12.1976. (Stay 
Application No. 6450 of 2009 stands disposed of). 
Summon the Lower Court Record. 
List after Lower Court Record is received. 
 
 (P.C.P., J.) 
29.07.2009
NS

Hon’ble Tarun Agarwala, J.
Mr. Sharad Sharma, Senior Advocate 
assisted by M. Jagdish Bisht, Advocate for the 
appellant 
Mr. Neeraj Garg, Advocate for the 
respondent. 
In the present appeal, the plaintiff and the 
defendant are brothers and there is a dispute with 
regard to partition of the property. Before the 
Court proceed the matter on merit, let an 
opportunity be given to the party to reconcile the 
matter between themselves through mediation. 
Therefore, the Court directs the parties, namely, 
the appellant and the defendant to appear before 
the mediation and conciliation center on 5th July, 
2010 for possible settlement. 
Let the matter be listed after the report of 
the mediation / conciliation center. 
(Tarun Agarwala, J.) 
Dated 15.06.2010

SA No. 41 of 2009
Hon'ble Prafulla C. Pant, J.
Shri Kamlesh Lohani, Advocate,
present for the appellant.
Shri Tapan Singh, Advocate, present
for the respondent.
This is Modification Application No.
13515 of 2011 moved on behalf of the third
party applicant Vijendra Kumar Goyal for
modification of interim order dated
29.07.2009, passed by this court.
Heard. 
The applicant Vijendra Kumar Goyal is
not a party in the appeal. Perusal of the
interim order dated 29.07.2009, clearly
shows that it is directed that the respondent
(in the appeal) i.e. Ram Niwas Goyal, shall
not create any third party interest in respect
of 50 percent share in the property
purchased through the sale deed dated
23.12.1976.
The interim order, in the above
circumstances, does not bind the third party.
Accordingly, the Modification Application
No. 13515 of 2011 is disposed of with the
clarification that the interim order passed in
this appeal is not directed against the third
party/applicant Vijendra Kumar Goyal. 
 
(P.C.Pant, J.)

orders.text:
SA 41/2009
Hon’ble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
Mr. T.A. Khan, Sr. Advocate, 
assisted by Mr. A.K. Arya, Advocate for 
the appellant. 
Mr. Arvind Vashistha, Sr. 
Advocate, assisted by Smt. Monika Pant, 
Advocate for the respondent. 
Having heard learned Sr. Counsel 
for the parties, it is evident that Mr. 
J.M. Singhal was the Counsel of the 
plaintiff in the trial court as well as 
before the first appellate court. First 
appeal was preferred by the plaintiff 
himself. Mr. Singhal had never filed his 
Vakalatnama on behalf of the 
defendant/respondent. Therefore, 
substantial question of law, formulated 
in this regard vide order dated 
29.7.2009, appears to have been framed 
under some misconception. Hence, the 
said substantial question of law is 
hereby recalled and, instead, following 
questions are framed for adjudication: 
(i) Whether once the registered 
document is not set aside by any 
competent court of law, the same should 
be read or relied as it is or not? 
(ii) Whether both the courts below 
erred in law in not accepting the 
concept of Joint Hindu Family regarding 
the joint property recorded in various 
records? 
If the need is felt at the time of 
arguments, additional substantial 
question(s) of law may be framed. 
Order dated 29.7.2009, passed by 
this Court, stands modified to the extent 
indicated above. The application moved 
therefor, on behalf of the respondent, 
stands disposed of accordingly. 
2018:UHC:2325 Application for adducing additional 
evidence (IA 2168/2012) is pending since 
long. Learned Sr. Counsel seeks time to 
file objections against this application. He 
could not file the same earlier as the case 
had to be heard on the said substantial 
question of law which was formulated 
under some misconception. 
As prayed for, two weeks’ time is 
granted to file such objections. 
List thereafter. 
 
 
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.) 
 25.4.2016 
 Prabodh

Reserved Judgment 
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL 
Second Appeal No.41 of 2009 
Reserved on: 17th February, 2018 
Decided on: 23rd March, 2018 
___________________________________________________
Ashok Kumar Goel (deceased) ..… Appellant 
Versus 
Ram Niwas Goel ...… Respondent
___________________________________________________
Mr. T.A. Khan, Senior Advocate, assisted by Mr. A.K. Arya, Advocate for the appellant. 
Mr. Arvind Vashistha, Senior Advocate, assisted by Ms. Monika Pant, Advocate for the respondent. 
Hon’ble Rajiv Sharma, J. 
 This regular second appeal is instituted against 
the judgment and decree dated 07.01.2008 rendered by 
learned Civil Judge (S.D.), Dehradun in Original Suit 
No.382 of 2004 as well as judgment dated 30.04.2009 
rendered by learned Additional District Judge, 5th Fast 
Track Court, Dehradun, in Civil Appeal No. 05 of 2008. 
2. Key facts, necessary for adjudication of this 
regular appeal, are that the appellant-plaintiff (hereinafter 
referred to as ‘plaintiff’ for convenience and brevity sake) 
filed a suit for partition against the respondent-defendant 
(hereinafter referred to as ‘defendant’ for convenience and 
brevity sake). According to the averments made in the 
plaint, the defendants are the brothers. The disputed 
property was purchased by the parties on 23.12.1976. 
The nature of the property is commercial as well as 
residential. The plaintiff suffered a severe heart attack in 
the year 1999. Thereafter, he again suffered second heart 
attack in the year 2002. The defendant has started 
raising construction on the property in dispute. The 
plaintiff objected to the same. The defendant also 
approached the police. He served a legal notice on the 
defendant on 26.06.2004. The defendant filed a written 
2018:UHC:2325 2
statement. He admitted that the parties were brothers. 
The oral partition had already taken place long back. 
They have got their respective shares and are in 
possession of the same. The property was bought by the 
defendant and his father late Sadhu Ram on 07.08.1976 
for consideration of Rs.68,500/-. The final payment of 
Rs.17,500/- was made by the defendant. The map was 
got approved in the year 1982. The entire property was 
partitioned. It was an oral partition. The replication was 
filed by the plaintiff. 
 3. The Trial Court framed the issues. The suit was 
dismissed by the learned Trial Court on 07.01.2008. The 
appeal filed by the plaintiff/appellant was also dismissed 
by the First Appellate Court on 30.04.2009. Hence, this 
regular second appeal. 
4. The regular second appeal was admitted on the 
following substantial question of law on 29.07.2009: - 
“Whether the act on the part of the counsel (Sri 
J.M. Singhal) who appeared earlier on behalf of 
appellant (plaintiff) in the suit and thereafter the 
said counsel appeared on behalf of respondent at 
the stage of first appeal, vitiated the entire 
proceedings before the first appellate court?” 
5. As far as framing of substantial question of law, at 
the time of admission of the regular second appeal, is 
concerned, it is not even a question of law. It could, at the 
most, be a case of professional misconduct and that too 
was required to be proved. In view of this, parties were 
permitted to advance the arguments on the issues arising 
from the pleadings and the oral and documentary 
evidence led by the parties qua partition. 
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties 
and gone through the judgment and record very carefully. 
7. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the 
appellant has vehemently argued that the Trial Court has 
2018:UHC:2325 3
not correctly appreciated the oral as well as documentary 
evidence which led to the miscarriage of justice. Learned 
counsel for the respondent has supported the judgments 
dated 07.01.2008 and 30.04.2009. 
8. The plaintiff has appeared as PW1 before the 
Trial Court. He led his evidence by way of filing the 
affidavit. According to his affidavit, the plaintiff was 
claiming partition only in respect of the property bearing 
no.4 New Road, Dehradun. It was residential and 
commercial in nature. He had suffered a heart attack in 
the month of March, 1999. He was hospitalized. He again 
suffered with the heart attack in the year 2002. The 
defendant started raising construction and made false 
representations to the M.D.D.A., Dehradun. He served 
legal notice to the defendant on 26.06.2004. He was cross 
examined. In his cross examination, he submitted that he 
was working in a medical store. He has not paid any tax. 
No partnership deed of Goel Medical Shop was ever 
prepared. He categorically admitted in his cross 
examination that initially, it was a joint family but now 
they are living separately. He has categorically admitted 
that there was oral family settlement. Both the brothers 
sat together and no third party was involved. On the basis 
of oral settlement, the partition has taken place. He has 
requested his brother to reduce the same to the writing 
but his brother did not agree to it. 
9. PW2 Smt. Sudesh Goyal has also led evidence 
by way of filing the affidavit. She is the wife of plaintiff. 
The averments made in the affidavit are the same which 
were made by the plaintiff in his affidavit. She was also 
cross examined. She admitted that the sale took place in 
the year 1976. Her husband started running an 
independent business since 1986. 
2018:UHC:2325 4
10. The defendant Ram Niwas Goyal has appeared 
as DW1. He has filed his affidavit. In Para-11 of the 
affidavit, he has categorically deposed that there was an 
oral partition. In his cross-examination, he has denied 
that no oral partition has taken place. 
11. The fact of the matter is that the plaintiff 
himself has admitted that there was an oral partition. 
Once he has made an admission, he cannot be permitted 
to resile out of his admission. 
12. Application under Order 41 Rule 27 of 
C.P.C. 
 The appellant submits that the arbitration has 
taken place qua joint Hindu family property and one 
Inder Singh was appointed as Arbitrator. He made an 
award on 29.03.1993. It was made a Rule of Court. It is 
not believable that the appellant was not aware of the 
award made in 29.03.1993. The purpose of Order 41 Rule 
27 C.P.C. is not to permit the parties to fill up the lacuna. 
 Accordingly, Application (I.A.) No. 2168 of 2012 
is dismissed. 
13. Accordingly, there is no merit in the regular 
Second Appeal and the same is hereby dismissed. 
 (Rajiv Sharma, J.) 
Jitendra
